frontmatter.title: Open-system simulation
frontmatter.description: A checked amplitude-damping dilation, reduced-state references and explicit environment/readout costs.

children.value: An environment can carry away information and energy, so a reduced system can evolve irreversibly even when the joint circuit is unitary. A dilation makes that interaction explicit; discarding every environment outcome produces the channel. Conditioning on an environment outcome would be a different operation.
This first open-system example implements a finite-time amplitude-damping channel with an actual two-qubit environment dilation. It belongs to the
. Its circuit, reduced state and observables are checked; general interacting Lindblad algorithms remain planned.

adds a noncommuting Hamiltonian with actual first/second-order channel schedules, fresh environments and an independent Liouvillian reference. The absorbing channel on this page remains its separately checked dissipative ingredient.

adds two-spin ZZ coupling, local X drives and local damping, with a global positive-time palindrome and an independent GKSL matrix check. Its measured energy and reset costs are analyzed in that method article.

The channel uses controlled RY and CX, with gate-based input preparation and a zero-input environment. Tests compare the actual gate circuit’s reduced density operator with an independent Kraus reference. The measured exports include resets, input preparation, basis changes and final measurements. A separate conditional physical-resource study below supplies actual Clifford+T compilation for the fixed default Z task. Hardware calibration, certified synthesis and general Liouvillian access remain unavailable.

children.value: The environment is traced/discarded for a retained-state output. The measured circuit instead measures both wires and ignores

environment outcome. It never postselects environment zero: conditioning on an environment result would implement a different task. An inverse dilation is not applied, since it would undo the intended system/environment interaction. Each independent trial begins with a freshly reset/prepared environment.

children.value: The actual circuit is evaluated with Qiskit Statevector/DensityMatrix and partial trace; the reference is formed independently with NumPy matrices and the finite-time formulas above. Those matrices are classical checks, not the quantum implementation. This particular finite-time dilation has no time-discretization approximation: with exact angles it realizes the stated one-jump channel. Tests cover four gate-prepared inputs at several times, arbitrary small mixed inputs, zero/full damping, the semigroup composition rule, positivity, trace and X/Y/Z means. They also check a two-system entangled input under the separately generated tensor product of two independent channels. Such bounded checks do not establish a general many-body algorithm or formal proof.

The complete known-input trial explicitly resets system and environment, prepares the named state, applies the dilation and measures both wires. X readout uses H before measurement; Y readout uses S-dagger then H; Z readout uses no basis rotation. The environment is measured in Z and its bit is ignored. Gate counts include these operations and the decomposition of CRY.

Channel approximation/representation, coherent synthesis, statistical error and physical faults remain separate. The ideal analytic channel has no time-step approximation; these original logical exports retain continuous-angle gates. A 0.05 observable-error proposal allocates 0.01 to channel bias, 0.01 to synthesis bias and 0.03 to sampling. The static shared resource adapter rejects explicit resets; the separate complete-instrument study below accounts for them under its own workload and physical model.

For each fixed rate/time, classical coefficient preparation evaluates exp, sqrt and atan2; the resulting coefficients are reused across trials.
